title: Behavioural and Emotional Signs

course_overview.overview: This lesson introduces the core ideas behind behavioural and emotional signs and prepares parents to apply the skills in real-life moments. It blends trauma-informed practice, relational safety, and practical strategies that can be used immediately[cite: 4].

learning_outcomes: Understand the purpose and value of behavioural and emotional signs[cite: 4].
Identify common challenges and how to respond calmly[cite: 4].
Practice simple, repeatable strategies that build confidence[cite: 4].
Strengthen connection and emotional safety during difficult moments[cite: 4].

behavioral_guidelines: Help parents decode stress behaviors without judgment[cite: 4].
Encourage reflective pausing and emotional processing[cite: 4].

facilitator_dialogue_flow.script: Welcome. Behavior is often a window into a child's inner world. Today we look at behavioral and emotional signs to understand what children are communicating through their actions.

key_concepts: Why behavioural and emotional signs matters for child development[cite: 4].
How trauma and stress impact behaviour[cite: 4].
How parents can model emotional regulation[cite: 4].
Predictability and routine as stabilising tools[cite: 4].
practice_activities: Try a 2-minute grounding exercise before responding to your child[cite: 4].
Practice naming emotions using simple, non-judgemental language[cite: 4].
Role-play a challenging moment and rehearse a calm script[cite: 4].
Identify one routine where behavioural and emotional signs can be used daily[cite: 4].
facilitator_notes: Normalise struggle — parents often feel shame around these skills[cite: 4].
Use examples that reflect diverse families and lived experiences[cite: 4].
Pause often for reflection and emotional processing[cite: 4].
Model co-regulation through tone, pacing, and presence[cite: 4].
reflection_prompts: What part of behavioural and emotional signs feels easiest for me?[cite: 4]
What part feels hardest, and why?[cite: 4]
How did my own childhood shape my reactions?[cite: 4]
What is one small change I can try this week?[cite: 4]
printable_summary:
behavioural and emotional signs — Key Takeaways:
- Stay calm and predictable[cite: 4].
- Use simple language[cite: 4].
- Focus on connection before correction[cite: 4].
- Practice small steps consistently[cite: 4].
